newsitem.title: CANADA: Kenting looking worldwide for rival bidder.
newsitem.headline: Kenting looking worldwide for rival bidder.

text.p: Kenting Energy Services Ltd, target of a takeover bid from Precision Drilling Corp, is scouring the globe in its quest for a higher offer, Kenting chief executive Tim Swinton said on Thursday.
"We've been actively seeking a suitor and we have canvassed the logical buyers on a global basis," Swinton said in a phone interview.

Kenting -- Canada's newest publicly traded oil and gas drilling firm -- has hired ScotiaMcleod Inc as adviser in the bid process, which was confirmed late Wednesday when Precision came back with an offer for both Kenting and Lynx Energy Services Corp.
Kenting and Lynx announced a merger moments after Precision revealed its play for Kenting early this month.
Swinton said he had no intention of selling his firm when it was spun off from Trimac Ltd one business day before the Precision bid was announced.

Precision said it would offer C$3.50 cash plus a 10th of a Precision share for each Kenting share, the same amount as its first plan. The bid now accounts for extra assets Kenting is acquiring with the Lynx merger.
If the price of Precision shares reached C$70, the bid would be valued at C$10.50 per Kenting share, a total of about C$500 million.
However, Precision shares have shed over C$11 since its first bid announcement.
At Thursday's closing Precision price of C$55.25, its bid would be valued at about C$9, below Kenting's current share price.
"We're not exactly sure where they are coming from with a bid that's a dollar under market," Swinton said.
Swinton said there had been no negotiations with Precision -- which would have a market share in Canada of almost 40 percent with Kenting under its wing -- on striking a friendly deal.
